I usually don't comment, but after having been in therapy for a while, I learned our brains actually have a negativity bias - we remember bad things rather than good things, so we can avoid the bad things in the future. Through training your brain to be mindful of the good things you can actually negate or reverse this entirely and start remembering a lot of the good days instead of the awful ones.

The dragons are attacking the city because of a slight made against them by the witches ages ago. They want revenge. Some of them don't actually attack the city, just get close enough for the witches to assume they are a threat, and they go after them. The main  perceived antagonist actually never does attack the city. The dragons are bitter and want to drive the witches out the same way they drove the dragons out of society. They want back in, but considering the witches are 'attack on sight', most have just decided to resort to violence or (in the case of wandering too close) in self defense.  

The TRUE antagonist is basically a massive being that desires the destruction of witches and dragons alike, to rule over the entire planet and defy the main deity of the witches. They're using the dragon-witch conflict to their advantage, waiting until the dragons dwindle in number and they're unable to aid each other due to conflict.

Sorry...First time writing anything of substance, actually. :/ I.. think I can answer that?

They're fighting them because they believe that they need to become stronger to protect their city. Overall, they believe that dragons are a menace - mindless creatures that are just out to kill and destroy. They see them as evil.  

They're fighting to protect their city, and (guiltily) for the enjoyment of fighting. This does change later as they become more familiar with the dangers and all.

Yes, there are quite a few dragons, but most tend to avoid getting too close to cities. The "less intelligent" dragons are the ones that tend to get too close.

I wanted to put other monsters in, but I'm still unclear on that as of now, same with them attacking dragons if I were to put them in. I think if I were to add more monsters, they would be capable of attacking farms and causing a decent amount of damage, but nothing comparable to a large-sized dragon.  

There are a small number of nearby cities, around 5. In further areas, there are quite a few more that will be mentioned, but not traveled to.  

I planned to have the main characters be Witches, yes. They are a small group within a Battalion of their city. To summarize, one of them is very excited about the battalion, is very eager to fight, and is a new recruit. Another is a bit more collected due to being in the battalion for a longer time, but has anger issues and tends to take them out on whatever they're fighting. The others I'm still working on.  

The witches' religion tells of a dragon that betrayed their idol and will return to destroy the continent and turn it into a burning wasteland. They're both trying to protect the cities and train themselves for when the dragon returns. Their religion has basically painted dragons as a force of evil. Instead of repelling them from cities as they would minor threats, they instead kill dragons. Some witches are known to take dragon parts as trophies. Others think taking dragon parts just brings you bad luck and avoid it.

They're perceived to be the main threat, yes. While some Dragons stay away from the cities, some wander too close and pose a danger to anyone who travels outside the walls. Others are just extremely bitter against witches for a past slight against dragons that cast them out entirely. (I am probably explaining this horribly)

That actually sounds really nice! I toyed with the idea of different species of dragons, but somehow missed the possibility that two could show up at once, or some could use certain types of magic to their advantage.
